name: Sign In with LinkedIn (OpenID Connect)
plain: Lets a site sign people in with their LinkedIn account and receive basic profile data.
meaning: After the person approves, the site gets a stable pairwise ID, name, photo, locale and optionally a verified email. It does not verify real world identity.

access.persistence: Access token lifetime set by LinkedIn; consent until revoked in LinkedIn settings
steps: Site redirects with scope openid profile email
Site exchanges the code for tokens (RS256 id_token, jwks at /oauth/openid/jwks)

limits.headline: Can sign you in with LinkedIn and get your name, photo and email
limits.user_action: You tap Sign in with LinkedIn and approve the LinkedIn consent screen
can: Receive a stable ID for you that is unique to that site
Get your name, photo, language and, if you allow, a verified email
Create or sign in to your account on that site
cannot: Prove who you are in real life
See your work history, connections or posts
Get anything beyond the permissions listed on the consent screen

story.what_it_is: Sign in with LinkedIn: you approve, and the site learns your name, photo and maybe email.
story.for_you: You are sent to a LinkedIn page that lists what the site wants (basic profile, email). You press Allow and you are sent back signed in. The site never sees your LinkedIn password.
story.for_makers: Makers of work apps skip password systems and get a real name and picture. Leads and trials arrive with cleaner data, and the site can personalize the first screen.

use_cases.example: A resume builder fills in a person's name, photo and email with one LinkedIn click, then offers to import their job history.
A webinar or whitepaper form is replaced with a LinkedIn sign in so the sales team gets a real contact.
An online course site signs in learners with LinkedIn so they can add a certificate to their profile.
An alumni or events platform imports names and photos so attendees look familiar in the guest list.
A career focused web game or hackathon portal uses it to register players with a real name.
B2B marketers use the verified email to match leads to ad campaigns and measure conversions.

technical_bounds: Subject is pairwise: not matchable across apps

linkedin.how: LinkedIn as identity provider for third party sites; part of the data flow around LinkedIn but not a fingerprinting method.
